```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcI")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0136369>

Taubel et al. (2015) re-analysed the electrocardiograms of a phase 1 single
ascending dose study of E-52862 (S1RA), an oral sigma-1 receptor antagonist
developed as an analgesic. Healthy adults received single oral doses of 500,
600 and 800 mg and placebo in a four-period crossover, each period preceded by a
placebo baseline day whose ECGs were time-matched to the dosing day. The paper
fits two series of linear mixed-effects concentration-QTc models (R `nlme`):

1. **Placebo-corrected change from baseline** (DeltaDeltaQTc) regressed on
   plasma concentration, with period, sequence and sex as fixed factors
   (Table 4).
2. **Change from baseline** (DeltaQTc) regressed on concentration with
   *nominal time* as an additional fixed factor and placebo entering at
   concentration 0 (Table 5). The time factor captures the QTc shortening that
   follows the standardised lunch at 5 h, which the authors use to demonstrate
   assay sensitivity (Table 7).

In both series the best model by AIC adds a random slope to the random
intercept. Each series was fitted for the individual (QTcI) and the Fridericia
(QTcF) correction, giving four packaged model files sharing this vignette:

| Model file | Endpoint | Structure | Source |
|------------|----------|-----------|--------|
| `Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcI` | DeltaDeltaQTcI (ms) | `e0 + slope * C` | Table 4 (slope), Table 6 (e0) |
| `Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcF` | DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms) | `e0 + slope * C` | Table 4 (slope), Table 6 (e0) |
| `Taubel_2015_E52862_dQTcI`  | DeltaQTcI (ms) | `e0 + theta(NTIME) + slope * C` | Table 5 (slope), Figure 5 (time course) |
| `Taubel_2015_E52862_dQTcF`  | change in DeltaQTcF from pre-dose (ms) | `theta(NTIME) + slope * C` | Table 5 (slope), Table 7 (6 h, 8 h) |

`C` is the covariate `CP_E52862_NGML`, the E-52862 (parent) plasma concentration
in ng/mL. The paper characterises the pharmacokinetics by non-compartmental
analysis only (Table 3), so these are PD-only models: the user supplies the
concentration. The same models were fitted for five metabolites (M1-M5), but
the paper reports numerical results only for the parent compound.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcI")()$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct", "race_ethnicity")])
```

Thirty-two healthy White, non-Hispanic adults (15 women, 47%) aged 18-35 years
with BMI 18-25 kg/m^2 were randomised; 31 completed all four periods (Taubel
2015 Table 2: age 24.22 +/- 4.668 years, weight 67.39 +/- 9.654 kg, BMI
22.41 +/- 1.643 kg/m^2). Triplicate ECGs and PK samples were taken at pre-dose
and 0.25-96 h after dosing; lunch was served at 5 h and dinner at 9 h on both
the baseline day and the dosing day.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| DeltaDeltaQTcI slope (model 2) | -0.00024 ms per ng/mL | Table 4, QTcI row 2 (best fit) |
| DeltaDeltaQTcF slope (model 2) | 0.00051 ms per ng/mL | Table 4, QTcF row 2 (best fit) |
| DeltaDeltaQTcI intercept `e0` | -1.53 ms | back-solved from Table 6, rows 1-3 |
| DeltaDeltaQTcF intercept `e0` | -1.58 ms | back-solved from Table 6, rows 4-6 |
| DeltaQTcI slope (model 2) | -0.00079 ms per ng/mL | Table 5, QTcI row 2 (best fit) |
| DeltaQTcF slope (model 2) | -0.00007 ms per ng/mL | Table 5, QTcF row 2 (best fit) |
| DeltaQTcI time course, 0-12 h | `e0` 0.9 ms and nine increments | digitised from Figure 5 |
| DeltaQTcF time effect at 6 h | -8.1 ms vs pre-dose | Table 7 |
| DeltaQTcF time effect at 8 h | -7.2 ms vs pre-dose | Table 7 |
| Model equations | linear in `C`, time as factor | Methods 'Statistical Methods' |
| IIV, residual error | not reported | typical-value models, `addSd = fixed(0)` |

```{r load-models}
mod_ddi <- readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcI")
mod_ddf <- readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_ddQTcF")
mod_di <- readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_dQTcI")
mod_df <- readModelDb("Taubel_2015_E52862_dQTcF")

# Typical-value prediction at a set of (concentration, nominal time) pairs.
# All rows sit in one subject at successive solver times; the models are
# algebraic, so solver time plays no role.
predict_qtc <- function(mod, conc, ntime = 0) {
  n <- max(length(conc), length(ntime))
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    time = seq_len(n),
    evid = 0L,
    amt = 0,
    CP_E52862_NGML = rep_len(conc, n),
    NTIME = rep_len(ntime, n)
  )
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev))
}
```

## Back-solving the DeltaDeltaQTc intercepts

The first-series models contain a fixed intercept and period, sequence and sex
effects that the paper does not print. Table 6, however, prints the model
prediction at the geometric-mean Cmax of each dose group. Holding the printed
slope, every intercept inside the interval below reproduces all three printed
predictions to their 0.1 ms rounding; the packaged `e0` is the interval centre.

```{r backsolve}
table6 <- data.frame(
  series = rep(c("DeltaDeltaQTc", "DeltaQTc"), each = 6),
  qtc = rep(rep(c("QTcI", "QTcF"), each = 3), 2),
  conc = rep(c(5464.0, 4302.4, 3859.6), 4),
  pred = c(-2.8, -2.6, -2.5, 1.2, 0.6, 0.4, -4.3, -3.4, -3.1, -0.4, -0.3, -0.3)
)

e0_interval <- function(slope, conc, pred) {
  c(lower = max(pred - 0.05 - slope * conc), upper = min(pred + 0.05 - slope * conc))
}
dd <- subset(table6, series == "DeltaDeltaQTc")
iv_i <- with(subset(dd, qtc == "QTcI"), e0_interval(-0.00024, conc, pred))
iv_f <- with(subset(dd, qtc == "QTcF"), e0_interval(0.00051, conc, pred))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Endpoint = c("DeltaDeltaQTcI", "DeltaDeltaQTcF"),
    `Lowest e0` = round(c(iv_i[["lower"]], iv_f[["lower"]]), 4),
    `Highest e0` = round(c(iv_i[["upper"]], iv_f[["upper"]]), 4),
    `Packaged e0` = c(-1.53, -1.58),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  caption = "Intercepts consistent with Taubel 2015 Table 6 at the printed slopes."
)
stopifnot(
  iv_i[["lower"]] < iv_i[["upper"]], iv_f[["lower"]] < iv_f[["upper"]],
  -1.53 >= iv_i[["lower"]], -1.53 <= iv_i[["upper"]],
  -1.58 >= iv_f[["lower"]], -1.58 <= iv_f[["upper"]]
)
```

# Virtual cohort

No virtual cohort is simulated. The paper reports neither the random-effect
variances nor the residual error, so the packaged models are typical-value
models and a stochastic cohort would add no information. The validation below
evaluates the models at the concentrations and nominal times the paper reports.

# Simulation and validation gate: Table 6

Table 6 prints twelve model predictions at the geometric-mean Cmax of each dose
group. This is a deterministic, zero-parameter gate: the only admissible
difference is the rounding of the printed slope (half a unit in the fifth
decimal, times the concentration), of the printed prediction (0.05 ms) and of
the two-decimal `e0` (0.005 ms).

```{r table6-gate}
mods <- list(
  DeltaDeltaQTc = list(QTcI = mod_ddi, QTcF = mod_ddf),
  DeltaQTc = list(QTcI = mod_di, QTcF = mod_df)
)
# The second-series predictions are the drug effect (slope * C), so they are
# evaluated as active minus placebo at the same nominal time.
gate <- table6
gate$model <- NA_real_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gate))) {
  m <- mods[[gate$series[i]]][[gate$qtc[i]]]
  out <- predict_qtc(m, conc = c(gate$conc[i], 0), ntime = 2)[[gate$qtc[i]]]
  gate$model[i] <- if (gate$series[i] == "DeltaQTc") out[1] - out[2] else out[1]
}
gate$diff <- gate$model - gate$pred
gate$tolerance <- 0.05 + 5e-6 * gate$conc + 0.005

gate |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 3), diff = round(diff, 3), tolerance = round(tolerance, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model series" = series, "QTc" = qtc, "Concentration (ng/mL)" = conc,
    "Paper (ms)" = pred, "Packaged model (ms)" = model, "Difference (ms)" = diff,
    "Rounding tolerance (ms)" = tolerance
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 6 of Taubel 2015.")

stopifnot(all(abs(gate$diff) <= gate$tolerance))
```

All twelve rows agree within rounding. The only row that does not re-round to
the printed digit is the DeltaQTcI prediction at 3859.6 ng/mL (-3.05 vs -3.1
ms): the printed slope -0.00079 is itself rounded, and any unrounded slope in
[-0.000796, -0.000790] reproduces all three DeltaQTcI rows.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4 -- DeltaDeltaQTcI against concentration

```{r figure4, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
conc_grid <- seq(0, 8000, by = 100)
fig4 <- rbind(
  data.frame(conc = conc_grid, value = predict_qtc(mod_ddi, conc_grid)$QTcI, endpoint = "DeltaDeltaQTcI"),
  data.frame(conc = conc_grid, value = predict_qtc(mod_ddf, conc_grid)$QTcF, endpoint = "DeltaDeltaQTcF")
)
ggplot(fig4, aes(conc, value, linetype = endpoint)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 10), colour = "grey60") +
  labs(
    x = "E-52862 plasma concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Placebo-corrected change (ms)",
    linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the regression line of Figure 4 of Taubel 2015 (typical value)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Both lines stay within a few milliseconds of zero across the observed
concentration range, far below the 10 ms threshold of regulatory concern.

## Figure 5 -- drug-free DeltaQTcI time course

Figure 5 overlays the time course estimated by six models (parent and the five
metabolites) without a legend. The packaged `dQTcI` time course is the mean of
the six curves at each nominal time; the band below is the range of the six
digitised curves.

```{r figure5, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
fig5_digitised <- data.frame(
  ntime = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12),
  low = c(0.2, -1.4, 0.2, 0.3, 0.0, -1.3, -1.0, -7.8, -6.8, -4.6),
  high = c(1.5, -0.3, 1.4, 1.9, 1.5, -0.1, 0.5, -6.0, -5.6, -3.1)
)
fig5_digitised$model <- predict_qtc(mod_di, conc = 0, ntime = fig5_digitised$ntime)$QTcI

ggplot(fig5_digitised, aes(ntime)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_line(aes(y = model)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = model)) +
  annotate("text", x = c(5, 9), y = 4, label = "meal") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 9), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(
    x = "Nominal time after dose (h)", y = "DeltaQTcI at C = 0 (ms)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Taubel 2015; band = range of the six digitised curves."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

stopifnot(all(fig5_digitised$model >= fig5_digitised$low - 1e-8 &
  fig5_digitised$model <= fig5_digitised$high + 1e-8))
```

## Table 7 -- assay sensitivity from the lunch effect

```{r table7}
tab7 <- data.frame(ntime = c(6, 8), paper = c(-8.1, -7.2), lower = c(-10.4, -9.4), upper = c(-5.9, -5.0))
tab7$dQTcF <- predict_qtc(mod_df, conc = 0, ntime = tab7$ntime)$QTcF
pre_i <- predict_qtc(mod_di, conc = 0, ntime = 0)$QTcI
tab7$dQTcI <- predict_qtc(mod_di, conc = 0, ntime = tab7$ntime)$QTcI - pre_i

tab7 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Nominal time (h)" = ntime, "Paper QTcF (ms)" = paper, "95% CI lower" = lower,
    "95% CI upper" = upper, "Packaged dQTcF (ms)" = dQTcF,
    "Packaged dQTcI, digitised (ms)" = dQTcI
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 7 of Taubel 2015 (change from pre-dose).")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(tab7$dQTcF - tab7$paper) < 1e-8),
  # The QTcI contrasts are not printed; the digitised Figure 5 time course
  # should still fall inside the QTcF confidence intervals.
  all(tab7$dQTcI > tab7$lower & tab7$dQTcI < tab7$upper)
)
```

The QTcF contrasts are the packaged parameters themselves. The QTcI contrasts
implied by the digitised Figure 5 (-7.8 and -7.0 ms) are close to the QTcF
values and inside their confidence intervals, consistent with the authors'
statement that both corrections show the post-prandial shortening.

## Illustrative day: placebo and 800 mg

The second-series model separates the drug effect from the meal-driven time
course. With the geometric-mean 800 mg Cmax held at every time point (a
deliberately conservative exposure; the paper reports no PK model to generate a
profile), the drug lowers QTcI by a further 4.3 ms at most.

```{r illustrative-day, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
nt <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12)
day <- rbind(
  data.frame(ntime = nt, arm = "placebo", QTcI = predict_qtc(mod_di, 0, nt)$QTcI),
  data.frame(ntime = nt, arm = "C = 5464 ng/mL", QTcI = predict_qtc(mod_di, 5464, nt)$QTcI)
)
ggplot(day, aes(ntime, QTcI, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Nominal time after dose (h)", y = "DeltaQTcI (ms)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Not applicable. The packaged models are PD-only concentration-effect models
with no dosing compartment or PK states; there is no simulated concentration-time
profile on which to run NCA. The paper's own NCA results (Table 3: Cmax 3938.5,
4357.9 and 5580.1 ng/mL; AUC0-inf 85754.7, 112069.7 and 155911.0 ng.h/mL after
500, 600 and 800 mg) describe the observed concentrations that drove the fits
and are recorded in the covariate notes.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Intercepts of the DeltaDeltaQTc models are back-solved.** The paper prints
  only the slopes (Table 4). The packaged `e0` (-1.53 ms QTcI, -1.58 ms QTcF)
  is the population-averaged sum of the fixed intercept and the period,
  sequence and sex effects, recovered from the Table 6 predictions as shown
  above. Individual period, sequence and sex effects cannot be recovered and
  are not represented.
- **The DeltaQTcI time course is digitised and approximate.** Figure 5 does not
  identify which of its six curves belongs to the parent model, so the
  packaged time effects are the mean of the six curves; the parent curve may
  differ by up to about 0.8 ms at any time point. Figure 5 shows only the
  0-12 h levels at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h; the model bins other
  `NTIME` values to the nearest plotted level and is not valid beyond 12 h.
- **The DeltaQTcF model is partial.** The paper reports QTcF time effects only
  as the 6 h and 8 h changes from pre-dose (Table 7). The file therefore
  returns the change from pre-dose, and at every other nominal time the time
  effect is set to zero; only the slope and the two meal contrasts are
  reproducible.
- **No random effects or residual error.** The best models include a random
  intercept and random slope per subject, but no variance is reported, so the
  models are typical-value models with `addSd = fixed(0)`.
- **Dose labels in Table 6.** In the first nine rows of Table 6 the dose-group
  labels are in reverse order: 5464.0 ng/mL is labelled 500 mg although it is
  the 800 mg geometric-mean Cmax (Table 3 arithmetic means 3938.5, 4357.9 and
  5580.1 ng/mL for 500, 600 and 800 mg; the last three rows are labelled
  correctly). The gate above uses the concentrations, which are unaffected.
- **Metabolites.** M1-M5 slopes are reported only qualitatively ("all the
  slopes ... were negative"), so no metabolite model is packaged.
- **Slope significance.** Only the DeltaQTcI slope (series 2) excludes zero; the
  others are compatible with no concentration effect. The paper concludes that
  E-52862 does not prolong QTc at single doses up to 800 mg.
